ppo_u120832: Stage-3 SELFPLAY, PufferLib 3.0 PPO (PuffeRL) fine-tune of s2_e1_s43 (winners-only BC). ~121k on-policy steps, 8 envs/8 workers, league mix (50% hot-reload mirror / 30% PRIOR / 20% public trio), terminal reward {0,0.5,1}, lr 3e-5 adam, masked Discrete(48). Rung-2: beats s2_e1_s43 head-to-head 87.5% [69.0-95.7], PRIOR 79.2%, own mid-run 62.5%; Glicko 1478+/-71 vs 1300+/-71 (non-overlap). Rung-3 clean (wins in 11 turns, no stalling). CPU rehearsal 3.9ms/decision, bundle 14 MiB.

s2_e1_s43: Stage-2 REWEIGHT winners-only BC (arm E1, seed 43). 3.32M-param option-scoring transformer, warm-started from the 3-epoch il_agent PRIOR, fine-tuned 12,900 steps @ LR 1e-4 cloning ONLY winning seats (winner_only filter over 822k rows). Rung-1: 75.9% top-1 held-out day (PRIOR 75.3%, majority 38.1%). Rung-2 pooled 3 seeds: E1 beats PRIOR head-to-head 62.5% [51.0-72.8]; 15-agent round-robin Glicko 1460. CPU rehearsal 4.4ms/decision, bundle 14 MiB.

Resubmit: agent_core_improved (AdvancedPolicy heuristic, USE_SEARCH=0 default) on Mega Lucario ex deck, unchanged from the build that scored 804.0 (55162376). Not the Alakazam-deck search ablation that scored 252.8/437.3 today (55190932/55190924) -- that was a deliberate, already-analyzed A0'' experiment, not a regression in this lineage. Not affected by the fallback-diagnostics/crash fixes in 449c67f either -- those touched benchmark_agents.py harness code and improved_probabilistic's deck-loading fallback, not this bundle's gameplay path.

agent_core_improved with real search (USE_SEARCH=1, rank_all()-based candidates, not the dead-bandit bug from 827.8) + BC prior (USE_BC_PRIOR=1, BC_PRIOR_C=0.75) piloting the Alakazam deck (agents/ryotasueyoshi_alakazam/deck.csv), forced on via main.py since HEAD defaults USE_SEARCH=0. Checkpoint models/il_agent (current, NOT the 827.8 checkpoint): sha256 bce726e56bb2e817c2e8ee18c37332089ef0597a00d5f5554b6e98d1d738e132, git f9a1b6f9e747e5bbc23db04b99d6bf20b6fbc472. Repo git SHA 8cf2dad9. Weaker local evidence than the companion pure-BC submission (il_agent_alakazam, same checkpoint/deck, no search): this config scored only 10.0% win rate [Wilson 95% CI 1.8,40.4] vs makthanithin_improved_prob (n=10), tied with/worse than the no-search control (20.0% [5.7,51.0]) at that sample size -- submitted anyway to get a real ladder read rather than assume the local benchmark predicts correctly. See notes/phase0_gate0_report.md (A0'' section).

il_agent (pure BC cloning, no search/heuristic) piloting the Alakazam deck (agents/ryotasueyoshi_alakazam/deck.csv) instead of the frozen Mega Lucario ex deck. Checkpoint models/il_agent (current, NOT the 827.8 checkpoint): sha256 bce726e56bb2e817c2e8ee18c37332089ef0597a00d5f5554b6e98d1d738e132, trained at git f9a1b6f9e747e5bbc23db04b99d6bf20b6fbc472 (epoch 2, step 38562, eval_acc 0.753 vs 0.381 majority). Repo git SHA 8cf2dad9. No BC prior / search involved -- the transformer scores options directly. Why: Alakazam's defining cards (Abra/Kadabra/Alakazam) appear in 16.1% (129/800) of BC-training-corpus perspectives vs 0.0% (0/800) for Mega Lucario ex/Riolu, so this checkpoint's card embeddings are actually trained for Alakazam. Local result: 62.5% win rate [Wilson 95% CI 38.6,81.5] vs makthanithin_improved_prob (n=16) and 62.5% [38.6,81.5] vs rule_baseline (n=16) -- statistically distinguishable from the same checkpoint's 0.0% [0.0,19.4] on the Lucario deck vs the same opponent. See notes/phase0_gate0_report.md (A0'' section) and reports/bc_standalone_deck_test.json.

improved_prob_main: clean from-scratch reimplementation of Ivan Ternovskiy's Improved Probabilistic agent (flat root Monte-Carlo/UCB1 search, top-8 heuristic candidates re-ranked via real engine rollouts). Top-ranked among our own agents in a 13-agent local round-robin (Glicko 1720.2, 64.3% win rate), ahead of agent_core_improved (1665.7).

agent_core_improved + BC prior: UCB1 search (existing proven agent) with the trained IL policy's softmax as a PUCT-style exploration bias. Degrades to plain search if torch/checkpoint unavailable -- verified via exec()-based isolation test both ways.
il_agent v1.1: fixed __file__ NameError under exec()-based validation loading (see prior ERROR submission); 3.3M-param BC, 73.0% top-1 offline vs 38.1% majority baseline
il_agent v1: 3.3M-param BC, 73.0% top-1 offline (vs 38.1% majority), loses to rule_baseline/agent_core_improved on Rung 2
